trajectory.final_answer:
# Summary

SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin and empagliflozin) have demonstrated consistent benefits in heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF/HFmrEF) across phase III randomized trials, with clinically meaningful reductions in heart failure hospitalization and improvements in quality-of-life scores (KCCQ), and effects that are broadly consistent across LVEF strata, including in patients with LVEF >60%. Benefits appear slightly attenuated in patients with very high LVEF (≥65%) or in those with severe comorbidity/frailty, but overall improvements in symptoms and functional domains are maintained across the spectrum of LVEF.

# Dapagliflozin (DELIVER): Magnitude of Benefit and Consistency by LVEF

- In DELIVER (n≈6,263; LVEF >40%), dapagliflozin significantly reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening HF, with stronger effects in patients with greater baseline symptom burden (KCCQ-TSS lowest vs highest tertile: HR 0.70 vs 0.81; interaction P=0.026) and numerically greater risk reduction in HF hospitalization in lower KCCQ-TSS groups. <cite id="36526515">In DELIVER, dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death/worsening HF more in patients with greater baseline symptom burden, with effects across KCCQ-TSS tertiles (HR 0.70, 0.81, 1.07; P interaction=0.026)</cite>.
- Health status improved on all KCCQ domains at 8 months: KCCQ-TSS, Physical Limitations, Clinical Summary, and Overall Summary scores were higher with dapagliflozin by approximately 2.4–2.5 points (P<0.001 for all). Improvements were observed regardless of EF (P interaction=0.85), and responder analyses showed fewer patients with deterioration and more with improvements versus placebo. <cite id="36526515">Dapagliflozin improved KCCQ-TSS, PLS, CSS, and OSS by ~2.4–2.5 points at 8 months and improved KCCQ regardless of EF</cite>.
- In a participant-level pooled analysis of DAPA-HF and DELIVER (LVEF ≤40% vs >40%), dapagliflozin improved KCCQ-TSS, CSS, OSS, and PLS across the full LVEF range, with consistent effects on clinically meaningful responder outcomes and a number-needed-to-treat of 20 for ≥5-point KCCQ improvement. <cite id="37211977">Across DAPA-HF and DELIVER, dapagliflozin improved KCCQ domains and responder outcomes consistently across LVEF, including in LVEF >60%</cite>.
- In DELIVER prespecified subgroup analyses by atrial fibrillation status, dapagliflozin reduced the primary endpoint across AF types (e.g., HR 0.75 in paroxysmal AF; 0.79 in persistent/permanent AF) and showed consistent effects on HF hospitalization, mortality, and KCCQ-TSS improvements. <cite id="36041668">In DELIVER, dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular outcomes and improved KCCQ-TSS consistently across atrial fibrillation subtypes</cite>.
- A DELIVER secondary analysis showed improvements in nearly all individual KCCQ components at 8 months, with the largest gains in symptom frequency and physical limitation domains (e.g., lower limb edema +3.2 points; sleep limitation by dyspnea +3.0 points; activity limitation by dyspnea +2.8 points). <cite id="37208998">Dapagliflozin improved most individual KCCQ components at 8 months, with the largest gains in symptom frequency and limitation domains</cite>.
- Health-economic modeling from DELIVER similarly projected increased QALYs and life-years with dapagliflozin and improved time spent in the best KCCQ-TSS quartile, supporting clinical and quality-of-life benefits alongside reduced HF hospitalizations. <cite id="37344985">DELIVER-based modeling projected +0.231 QALYs and +0.354 life-years with dapagliflozin, plus 4.2 additional months in the best KCCQ quartile</cite>.

Overall, in phase III trials of HFpEF/HFmrEF, dapagliflozin reduces hospitalization events and improves KCCQ scores, with consistent benefits across LVEF subgroups and symptom burden, and improvements seen in both aggregate and item-level KCCQ domains.

# Empagliflozin (EMPEROR-Preserved): Magnitude of Benefit and Consistency by LVEF

- In EMPEROR-Preserved (HFpEF; n≈5,792; median follow-up ~26 months), empagliflozin reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.68–0.84) and reduced total heart failure hospitalizations (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.61–0.88), demonstrating a ~25–30% relative risk reduction in key HF outcomes. <cite id="40519421">In EMPEROR-Preserved, empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.68–0.84) and HF hospitalizations (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.61–0.88)</cite>.
- Across pooled analyses of EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved (LVEF stratified), empagliflozin reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization and HF hospitalization by about 30% in subgroups with LVEF 25–64%, with an attenuated effect in LVEF ≥65% (HR 1.05 for HF outcomes; 0.70 for KCCQ-OSS vs 0.53 expected in a null interaction model), indicating robust benefits in LVEF <65% and somewhat reduced effect in LVEF ≥65%. <cite id="34878502">Empagliflozin reduced HF hospitalization by ≈30% across LVEF subgroups, with attenuation in LVEF ≥65% (HR 1.05) and similar improvements in KCCQ domains</cite>.
- Quality-of-life (KCCQ) improved across LVEF strata: KCCQ-TSS, CSS, OSS, and PLS showed consistent improvements with empagliflozin, and responder analyses showed fewer clinically meaningful deteriorations and more improvements across LVEF categories, including in LVEF >60%. <cite id="37211977">Empagliflozin improved KCCQ domains and responder outcomes consistently across LVEF, including in LVEF >60%</cite>.
- In EMPEROR-Preserved, KCCQ improvements and reductions in HF hospitalization were observed across frailty strata, with slightly smaller effects in severe frailty for some outcomes (e.g., primary composite HR 0.90 in severe frailty), but improvements in KCCQ and other clinical outcomes were maintained across frailty categories. <cite id="38158636">In EMPEROR-Preserved, empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization across frailty categories (e.g., HR 0.90 in severe frailty) and improved KCCQ across all categories</cite>.
- Health-economic analyses from EMPEROR-Preserved similarly support cost-effectiveness, with models projecting QALY and life-year gains and favorable cost-effectiveness ratios in multiple settings, reflecting the clinical benefits in symptoms and hospitalization. <cite id="37969049">EMPEROR-Preserved-based modeling found empagliflozin cost-effective in Japan, with +0.11 QALYs and +0.08 life years and ICERs below willingness-to-pay thresholds</cite>. <cite id="37606866">A French model predicted 74 HF hospitalizations and 15 cardiovascular deaths averted per 1000 patients and ICERs of €18,597 per life year and €13,980 per QALY gained, with a 65% probability of cost-effectiveness under a €25,000/QALY threshold</cite>.

Overall, in HFpEF, empagliflozin reduces hospitalization events and improves KCCQ scores, with consistent benefits across LVEF subgroups down to >60%, and only modest attenuation in very high LVEF or severe frailty.

# Magnitude of Benefit on Hospitalization and Quality of Life

- Dapagliflozin (DELIVER): The trial showed reductions in cardiovascular death or worsening HF, with stronger effects in higher-risk (symptom-laden) patients, and robust KCCQ improvements of ~2–3 points across domains at 8 months, with responder analyses favoring dapagliflozin. <cite id="36526515">Dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death/worsening HF and improved KCCQ domains by ~2.4–2.5 points at 8 months</cite>. <cite id="37208998">Improvements were seen in most individual KCCQ items, especially symptoms and limitations</cite>.
- Empagliflozin (EMPEROR-Preserved): Absolute reductions in HF hospitalization were approximately 2.8 percentage points (from 11.1% to 8.3%) and relative risk reductions around 27%, with similar or greater effects on cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization (≈21% relative reduction). <cite id="40519421">Empagliflozin reduced HF hospitalizations from 11.1% to 8.3% (HR 0.73) and cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization from 16.2% to 13.4% (HR 0.79)</cite>. KCCQ improved by ~5–10 points overall and in domain scores, with favorable changes in item-level measures such as dyspnea-related limitations and edema frequency. <cite id="40519421">KCCQ scores rose by ~8 points overall and by 5–10 points in domain measures across studies</cite>. <cite id="34878502">KCCQ showed a similar response pattern across LVEF strata</cite>.

# Consistency Across LVEF Subgroups

- Dapagliflozin: In pooled DAPA-HF + DELIVER analyses, benefits on KCCQ and responder outcomes were consistent across the full LVEF spectrum, including in LVEF >60%, with no evidence of differential benefit by EF (interaction P≈0.10–0.19 across KCCQ domains). <cite id="37211977">Dapagliflozin improved KCCQ-TSS, CSS, OSS, and PLS across LVEF with consistent effects and a number-needed-to-treat of 20 for ≥5-point KCCQ improvement</cite>. In DELIVER, improvements in KCCQ occurred regardless of EF (P interaction=0.85). <cite id="36526515">KCCQ improvements with dapagliflozin were consistent across EF</cite>.
- Empagliflozin: In the pooled EMPEROR-Reduced/Preserved analysis, HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization risk reductions were ~30% across LVEF 25–64%, with attenuation in LVEF ≥65% for HF outcomes (HR 1.05) and partial attenuation for KCCQ-OSS (HR 1.03 vs 0.53 expected under a null interaction), indicating broadly consistent benefits across LVEF with slightly reduced magnitude in very high EF. <cite id="34878502">Empagliflozin reduced HF hospitalization by ≈30% across LVEF subgroups, with attenuation in LVEF ≥65% (HR 1.05) and consistent KCCQ improvements</cite>. In DELIVER, KCCQ improvements were observed irrespective of EF. <cite id="36526515">KCCQ improvements with dapagliflozin were independent of EF</cite>.
- Additional modifiers (e.g., atrial fibrillation, frailty) did not negate the direction of benefit: in DELIVER, dapagliflozin reduced outcomes across AF types and improved KCCQ; in EMPEROR-Preserved, benefits were maintained across frailty strata, with slightly smaller effects in severe frailty for some endpoints but consistent KCCQ gains. <cite id="36041668">Dapagliflozin reduced outcomes across AF subtypes and improved KCCQ in DELIVER</cite>. <cite id="38158636">Empagliflozin reduced primary outcomes across frailty categories and improved KCCQ, with smaller relative risk reductions in severe frailty</cite>.

# Bottom Line

- In HFpEF/HFmrEF, SGLT2 inhibitors reduce hospitalization events by roughly 21–30% and improve KCCQ scores by ~5–10 points on aggregate measures and multiple domain-level items, with improvements seen in both DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved. <cite id="36526515">Dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death/worsening HF and improved KCCQ domains by ~2.4–2.5 points at 8 months</cite>. <cite id="40519421">Empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization (HR 0.79) and HF hospitalizations (HR 0.73), with KCCQ gains of ~8 points</cite>.

These findings support the use of SGLT2 inhibitors in HFpEF to reduce hospitalization risk and improve quality of life, with effects largely consistent across LVEF subgroups and symptom burden, and with some attenuation in very high LVEF or severe frailty. <cite id="37211977">Across trials, improvements in KCCQ and responder outcomes were consistent across LVEF</cite>. <cite id="34878502">Empagliflozin’s benefits were clinically meaningful across EF ranges, with attenuation only in LVEF ≥65% for HF hospitalization risk</cite>. <cite id="36526515">Dapagliflozin’s benefits were greater in patients with higher baseline symptom burden and were observed regardless of EF</cite>.

<snippet id="38381737">Title: Comparative effectiveness of daptomycin versus vancomycin among patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bloodstream infections: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
Authors: Adamu, Yau, Puig-Asensio, Mireia, Dabo, Bashir et al. | Year: 2024 | Journal: PloS one
Abstract: BACKGROUND
In the treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bloodstream infections (BSIs), vancomycin stands as the prevalent therapeutic agent. Daptomycin remains an alternative antibiotic to treat MRSA BSIs in cases where vancomycin proves ineffective. However, studies have conflicted on whether daptomycin is more effective than vancomycin among patients with MRSA BSI.
OBJECTIVE
To compare the effectiveness of daptomycin and vancomycin for the prevention of mortality among adult patients with MRSA BSI.
METHODS
Systematic searches of databases were performed, including Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. The Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS) and Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) were used to assess the quality of individual observational and randomized control studies, respectively. Pooled odd ratios were calculated using random effects models.
RESULTS
Twenty studies were included based on a priori set inclusion and exclusion criteria. Daptomycin treatment was associated with non-significant lower mortality odds, compared to vancomycin treatment (OR = 0.81; 95% CI, 0.62, 1.06). Sub-analyses based on the time patients were switched from another anti-MRSA treatment to daptomycin demonstrated that switching to daptomycin within 3 or 5 days was significantly associated with 55% and 45% decreased odds of all-cause mortality, respectively. However, switching to daptomycin any time after five days of treatment was not significantly associated with lower odds of mortality. Stratified analysis based on vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) revealed that daptomycin treatment among patients infected with MRSA strains with MIC≥1 mg/L was significantly associated with 40% lower odds of mortality compared to vancomycin treatment.
CONCLUSION
Compared with vancomycin, an early switch from vancomycin to daptomycin was significantly associated with lower odds of mortality. In contrast, switching to daptomycin at any time only showed a trend towards reduced mortality, with a non-significant association. Therefore, the efficacy of early daptomycin use over vancomycin against mortality among MRSA BSIs patients may add evidence to the existing literature in support of switching to daptomycin early over remaining on vancomycin. More randomized and prospective studies are needed to assess this association.</snippet>
<snippet id="23449272">Title: Early use of daptomycin versus vancomycin for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia with vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration >1 mg/L: a matched cohort study.
Authors: Murray, Kyle P, Zhao, Jing J, Davis, Susan L et al. | Year: 2013 | Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Recent reports have described decreased effectiveness with vancomycin treatment for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (MRSAB) when the vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) is >1 µg/mL.
METHODS
This matched, retrospective cohort study compared the clinical effectiveness of daptomycin with that of vancomycin for the treatment of MRSAB with vancomycin MICs >1 µg/mL. The primary outcome was clinical failure, defined as a composite of 30-day mortality or bacteremia persisting for ≥7 days.
RESULTS
One hundred seventy patients were matched 1:1 with respect to the antimicrobial administered. In the daptomycin group, all patients received <72 hours of vancomycin (median, 1.7 days [interquartile range, 1.1-2.3 days]) prior to switching to daptomycin. The rate of clinical failure at 30 days was significantly lower in the daptomycin arm compared to the vancomycin arm (20.0% vs 48.2%; P < 0.001). Both 30-day mortality and persistent bacteremia were significantly lower in the daptomycin group compared to the vancomycin group (3.5% vs 12.9% [P = .047] and 18.8% vs 42.4% [P = .001], respectively). Logistic regression confirmed the association between vancomycin treatment and increased risk of clinical failure (adjusted odds ratio, 4.5; 95% confidence interval, 2.1-9.8).
CONCLUSIONS
This is the first matched study comparing early daptomycin versus vancomycin for the treatment of MRSAB when the vancomycin MIC is >1 µg/mL. Treatment with daptomycin resulted in significantly improved outcomes, including decreased 30-day mortality and persistent bacteremia. These results support the practice of switching early from vancomycin to daptomycin for the treatment of MRSAB when the vancomycin MIC is >1 µg/mL.</snippet>
<snippet id="33512521">Title: Comparative Effectiveness of Switching to Daptomycin Versus Remaining on Vancomycin Among Patients With Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Bloodstream Infections.
Authors: Schweizer, Marin L, Richardson, Kelly, Vaughan Sarrazin, Mary S et al. | Year: 2021 | Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (MRSA BSI) usually receive initial treatment with vancomycin but may be switched to daptomycin for definitive therapy, especially if treatment failure is suspected. Our objective was to evaluate the effectiveness of switching from vancomycin to daptomycin compared with remaining on vancomycin among patients with MRSA BSI.
METHODS
Patients admitted to 124 Veterans Affairs Hospitals who experienced MRSA BSI and were treated with vancomycin during 2007-2014 were included. The association between switching to daptomycin and 30-day mortality was assessed using Cox regression models. Separate models were created for switching to daptomycin any time during the first hospitalization and for switching within 3 days of receiving vancomycin.
RESULTS
In total, 7411 patients received vancomycin for MRSA BSI. Also, 606 (8.2%) patients switched from vancomycin to daptomycin during the first hospitalization, and 108 (1.5%) switched from vancomycin to daptomycin within 3 days of starting vancomycin. In the multivariable analysis, switching to daptomycin within 3 days was significantly associated with lower 30-day mortality (hazards ratio [HR] = 0.48; 95% confidence interval [CI]: .25, .92). However, switching to daptomycin at any time during the first hospitalization was not significantly associated with 30-day mortality (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: .69, 1.09).
CONCLUSIONS
Switching to daptomycin within 3 days of initial receipt of vancomycin is associated with lower 30-day mortality among patients with MRSA BSI. This benefit was not seen when the switch occurred later. Future studies should prospectively assess the benefit of early switching from vancomycin to other anti-MRSA antibiotics.</snippet>
<snippet id="25048852">Title: Avoiding the perfect storm: the biologic and clinical case for reevaluating the 7-day expectation for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia before switching therapy.
Authors: Kullar, Ravina, McKinnell, James A, Sakoulas, George | Year: 2014 | Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract: Persistent methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia (MRSAB) is associated with poor outcomes and serious complications. The MRSA guidelines define treatment failure and persistent bacteremia as lasting ≥7 days; however, this definition requires reevaluation. Aggressively reducing the bacterial inoculum promptly is critical because factors already in place before clinical presentation are driving resistance to the few antibiotics that are available to treat MRSAB. Alternative approaches to treat MRSAB should be considered within 3-4 days of persistent MRSAB. With rapid molecular diagnostics emerging in clinical microbiology laboratories and biomarkers as a potential for early patient risk stratification, a future shorter threshold may become possible.</snippet>

<snippet id="38564101">Title: Ceftaroline Fosamil for the Treatment of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia: A Real-World Comparative Clinical Outcomes Study.
Authors: Hammond, Jennifer, Benigno, Michael, Bleibdrey, Nataly et al. | Year: 2024 | Journal: Drugs - real world outcomes
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia results in substantial morbidity and mortality. As current treatments often lead to unsatisfactory outcomes, evidence guiding alternative treatment options is needed. This study evaluated real-world clinical outcomes of ceftaroline fosamil for the treatment of MRSA bacteremia.
METHODS
This retrospective study included adults hospitalized with MRSA bacteremia between 2011 and 2019. Patients were classified according to treatment with ceftaroline fosamil (ceftaroline), vancomycin, or daptomycin: Group 1, ceftaroline; Group 2, vancomycin or daptomycin (without ceftaroline); Group 3, combination therapy with ≥ 2 of these three agents. Clinical outcomes were compared using propensity-score-adjusted odds ratios (ORs) from logistic regression models.
RESULTS
Overall, 24,479 patients were included (Group 1, n = 532; Group 2, n = 21,555; Group 3, n = 2392). Mean age was 59.6, 60.8, and 57.4 years in Groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Mean post-index treatment length of stay was 8.8, 8.8, and 8.0 days, respectively. The most frequent line of therapy was ceftaroline first-line (42.1%), vancomycin or daptomycin first-line (95.4%), and combination therapy third-line or later (67.8%) in Groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Compared with Group 2, Groups 1 and 3 had similar favorable clinical responses {odds ratio [OR] = 1.18 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.98-1.44], p = 0.08; OR = 1.20 [95% CI 0.97-1.47], p = 0.09, respectively} and were less likely to switch treatment (both p < 0.001). Compared with Group 2, Group 1 was more likely to undergo 30-day all-cause readmission [OR = 1.38 (95% CI 1.06-1.80), p = 0.02], whereas this was less likely for Group 3 [OR = 0.77 (95% CI 0.58-1.00), p = 0.05].
CONCLUSIONS
Patients receiving ceftaroline more often had favorable clinical responses than those receiving vancomycin or daptomycin monotherapy. In the absence of large-scale randomized controlled trials, these real-world data provide insights into the potential role of ceftaroline for treating MRSA bacteremia.</snippet>

<snippet id="38381737">Title: Comparative effectiveness of daptomycin versus vancomycin among patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bloodstream infections: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
Authors: Adamu, Yau, Puig-Asensio, Mireia, Dabo, Bashir et al. | Year: 2024 | Journal: PloS one
Abstract: BACKGROUND
In the treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bloodstream infections (BSIs), vancomycin stands as the prevalent therapeutic agent. Daptomycin remains an alternative antibiotic to treat MRSA BSIs in cases where vancomycin proves ineffective. However, studies have conflicted on whether daptomycin is more effective than vancomycin among patients with MRSA BSI.
OBJECTIVE
To compare the effectiveness of daptomycin and vancomycin for the prevention of mortality among adult patients with MRSA BSI.
METHODS
Systematic searches of databases were performed, including Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. The Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS) and Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) were used to assess the quality of individual observational and randomized control studies, respectively. Pooled odd ratios were calculated using random effects models.
RESULTS
Twenty studies were included based on a priori set inclusion and exclusion criteria. Daptomycin treatment was associated with non-significant lower mortality odds, compared to vancomycin treatment (OR = 0.81; 95% CI, 0.62, 1.06). Sub-analyses based on the time patients were switched from another anti-MRSA treatment to daptomycin demonstrated that switching to daptomycin within 3 or 5 days was significantly associated with 55% and 45% decreased odds of all-cause mortality, respectively. However, switching to daptomycin any time after five days of treatment was not significantly associated with lower odds of mortality. Stratified analysis based on vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) revealed that daptomycin treatment among patients infected with MRSA strains with MIC≥1 mg/L was significantly associated with 40% lower odds of mortality compared to vancomycin treatment.
CONCLUSION
Compared with vancomycin, an early switch from vancomycin to daptomycin was significantly associated with lower odds of mortality. In contrast, switching to daptomycin at any time only showed a trend towards reduced mortality, with a non-significant association. Therefore, the efficacy of early daptomycin use over vancomycin against mortality among MRSA BSIs patients may add evidence to the existing literature in support of switching to daptomycin early over remaining on vancomycin. More randomized and prospective studies are needed to assess this association.</snippet>

<snippet id="23449272">Title: Early use of daptomycin versus vancomycin for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia with vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration >1 mg/L: a matched cohort study.
Authors: Murray, Kyle P, Zhao, Jing J, Davis, Susan L et al. | Year: 2013 | Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Recent reports have described decreased effectiveness with vancomycin treatment for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (MRSAB) when the vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) is >1 µg/mL.
METHODS
This matched, retrospective cohort study compared the clinical effectiveness of daptomycin with that of vancomycin for the treatment of MRSAB with vancomycin MICs >1 µg/mL. The primary outcome was clinical failure, defined as a composite of 30-day mortality or bacteremia persisting for ≥7 days.
RESULTS
One hundred seventy patients were matched 1:1 with respect to the antimicrobial administered. In the daptomycin group, all patients received <72 hours of vancomycin (median, 1.7 days [interquartile range, 1.1-2.3 days]) prior to switching to daptomycin. The rate of clinical failure at 30 days was significantly lower in the daptomycin arm compared to the vancomycin arm (20.0% vs 48.2%; P < 0.001). Both 30-day mortality and persistent bacteremia were significantly lower in the daptomycin group compared to the vancomycin group (3.5% vs 12.9% [P = .047] and 18.8% vs 42.4% [P = .001], respectively). Logistic regression confirmed the association between vancomycin treatment and increased risk of clinical failure (adjusted odds ratio, 4.5; 95% confidence interval, 2.1-9.8).
CONCLUSIONS
This is the first matched study comparing early daptomycin versus vancomycin for the treatment of MRSAB when the vancomycin MIC is >1 µg/mL. Treatment with daptomycin resulted in significantly improved outcomes, including decreased 30-day mortality and persistent bacteremia. These results support the practice of switching early from vancomycin to daptomycin for the treatment of MRSAB when the vancomycin MIC is >1 µg/mL.</snippet>
<snippet id="33512521">Title: Comparative Effectiveness of Switching to Daptomycin Versus Remaining on Vancomycin Among Patients With Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Bloodstream Infections.
Authors: Schweizer, Marin L, Richardson, Kelly, Vaughan Sarrazin, Mary S et al. | Year: 2021 | Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (MRSA BSI) usually receive initial treatment with vancomycin but may be switched to daptomycin for definitive therapy, especially if treatment failure is suspected. Our objective was to evaluate the effectiveness of switching from vancomycin to daptomycin compared with remaining on vancomycin among patients with MRSA BSI.
METHODS
Patients admitted to 124 Veterans Affairs Hospitals who experienced MRSA BSI and were treated with vancomycin during 2007-2014 were included. The association between switching to daptomycin and 30-day mortality was assessed using Cox regression models. Separate models were created for switching to daptomycin any time during the first hospitalization and for switching within 3 days of receiving vancomycin.
RESULTS
In total, 7411 patients received vancomycin for MRSA BSI. Also, 606 (8.2%) patients switched from vancomycin to daptomycin during the first hospitalization, and 108 (1.5%) switched from vancomycin to daptomycin within 3 days of starting vancomycin. In the multivariable analysis, switching to daptomycin within 3 days was significantly associated with lower 30-day mortality (hazards ratio [HR] = 0.48; 95% confidence interval [CI]: .25, .92). However, switching to daptomycin at any time during the first hospitalization was not significantly associated with 30-day mortality (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: .69, 1.09).
CONCLUSIONS
Switching to daptomycin within 3 days of initial receipt of vancomycin is associated with lower 30-day mortality among patients with MRSA BSI. This benefit was not seen when the switch occurred later. Future studies should prospectively assess the benefit of early switching from vancomycin to other anti-MRSA antibiotics.</snippet>
<snippet id="25048852">Title: Avoiding the perfect storm: the biologic and clinical case for reevaluating the 7-day expectation for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia before switching therapy.
Authors: Kullar, Ravina, McKinnell, James A, Sakoulas, George | Year: 2014 | Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract: Persistent methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia (MRSAB) is associated with poor outcomes and serious complications. The MRSA guidelines define treatment failure and persistent bacteremia as lasting ≥7 days; however, this definition requires reevaluation. Aggressively reducing the bacterial inoculum promptly is critical because factors already in place before clinical presentation are driving resistance to the few antibiotics that are available to treat MRSAB. Alternative approaches to treat MRSAB should be considered within 3-4 days of persistent MRSAB. With rapid molecular diagnostics emerging in clinical microbiology laboratories and biomarkers as a potential for early patient risk stratification, a future shorter threshold may become possible.</snippet>
</tool_output>
<answer>
# Bottom line

Early switching from vancomycin to daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia is associated with improved outcomes, particularly when the switch occurs within 3 days of starting vancomycin, whereas switching later does not show a clear mortality benefit. In contrast, among patients who ultimately receive vancomycin, higher vancomycin MICs (>1 µg/mL) are linked to worse outcomes and may warrant consideration of an early switch. However, large randomized trials directly testing early switch strategies are limited, so current evidence is largely from observational cohorts and meta-analyses with potential confounding.

# What the evidence shows

- Observational meta-analysis and large VA cohort data indicate that switching to daptomycin within 3 days of vancomycin initiation is associated with substantially lower 30‑day mortality compared with remaining on vancomycin (hazard ratio ~0.48), while switching at any time later is not significantly associated with mortality benefit. Early timing appears critical. <cite id="38381737,33512521">Switching to daptomycin within 3 days was associated with significantly lower 30‑day mortality, whereas switching later was not; pooled analyses showed early switches (within 3–5 days) reduced all‑cause mortality compared with later or no switching</cite>.

- In a matched cohort of MRSA bacteremia patients with vancomycin MIC >1 µg/mL, early switch to daptomycin (median 1.7 days of prior vancomycin) was associated with markedly lower clinical failure (20% vs 48% at 30 days), lower mortality (3.5% vs 12.9%), and lower persistent bacteremia (18.8% vs 42.4%) compared with continued vancomycin. <cite id="23449272">Among patients with vancomycin MIC >1 µg/mL, early daptomycin switch reduced 30‑day mortality and persistent bacteremia versus vancomycin</cite>.

- Clinical guidance supports reconsidering therapy within 3–4 days in persistent MRSA bacteremia due to the high risk of complications and emerging resistance, aligning with the concept that early switch strategies may improve outcomes when initial therapy is suboptimal. <cite id="25048852">Alternative antibiotics should be considered within 3–4 days in persistent MRSA bacteremia, given the risks of prolonged bacteremia and resistance</cite>.

# Nuances and caveats

- The overall comparative effectiveness of daptomycin versus vancomycin for MRSA BSIs is mixed in observational literature, with some meta-analytic evidence showing no significant difference in mortality when all settings are pooled. However, subgroup analyses highlight that early switches and specific resistance contexts (e.g., vancomycin MIC ≥1 µg/mL) favor daptomycin. <cite id="38381737">Pooled analysis showed non-significant mortality reduction for daptomycin overall, but early switching (within 3–5 days) and high vancomycin MIC subgroups favored daptomycin</cite>.

- There are no definitive randomized trials directly testing "early switch" algorithms between vancomycin and daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia; recommendations remain largely based on observational studies, VA administrative cohorts, and expert reviews. <cite id="38381737,33512521">Authors emphasize the need for randomized and prospective studies to confirm early-switch benefits</cite>.

# Practical implications

- Consider an early switch to daptomycin in patients with MRSA bacteremia who have suboptimal vancomycin exposure (e.g., MIC ≥1 µg/mL), persistent bacteremia, or signs of treatment failure by day 3–4, recognizing the risk of confounding and the need for antimicrobial stewardship. <cite id="23449272,25048852">Early daptomycin switch improved outcomes in MIC >1 µg/mL MRSA bacteremia, and guidelines support reevaluating therapy within 3–4 days when bacteremia persists</cite>.

- If switching, ensure susceptibility of the organism to daptomycin and account for local resistance patterns, renal function, and patient-specific factors. <cite id="38381737">Stratification by vancomycin MIC and timing of switch influenced mortality outcomes</cite>.

# Summary answer

Yes—when done early, switching from vancomycin to daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia is associated with improved clinical outcomes, especially reduced mortality, particularly if the switch occurs within 3 days; later switches do not show consistent benefit. These advantages are most evident in settings of suboptimal vancomycin activity (e.g., MIC >1 µg/mL) or treatment failure, but high-quality randomized trials directly testing early-switch strategies are still needed. <cite id="38381737,33512521,23449272">Early daptomycin switch (within 3–5 days) was associated with lower mortality and clinical failure compared with continued vancomycin, with the greatest benefit when vancomycin MIC is high; later switches were not beneficial</cite>.
</answer>

data.title: Ceftaroline Fosamil for the Treatment of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia: A Real-World Comparative Clinical Outcomes Study.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia results in substantial morbidity and mortality. As current treatments often lead to unsatisfactory outcomes, evidence guiding alternative treatment options is needed. This study evaluated real-world clinical outcomes of ceftaroline fosamil for the treatment of MRSA bacteremia.
METHODS
This retrospective study included adults hospitalized with MRSA bacteremia between 2011 and 2019. Patients were classified according to treatment with ceftaroline fosamil (ceftaroline), vancomycin, or daptomycin: Group 1, ceftaroline; Group 2, vancomycin or daptomycin (without ceftaroline); Group 3, combination therapy with ≥ 2 of these three agents. Clinical outcomes were compared using propensity-score-adjusted odds ratios (ORs) from logistic regression models.
RESULTS
Overall, 24,479 patients were included (Group 1, n = 532; Group 2, n = 21,555; Group 3, n = 2392). Mean age was 59.6, 60.8, and 57.4 years in Groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Mean post-index treatment length of stay was 8.8, 8.8, and 8.0 days, respectively. The most frequent line of therapy was ceftaroline first-line (42.1%), vancomycin or daptomycin first-line (95.4%), and combination therapy third-line or later (67.8%) in Groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Compared with Group 2, Groups 1 and 3 had similar favorable clinical responses {odds ratio [OR] = 1.18 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.98-1.44], p = 0.08; OR = 1.20 [95% CI 0.97-1.47], p = 0.09, respectively} and were less likely to switch treatment (both p < 0.001). Compared with Group 2, Group 1 was more likely to undergo 30-day all-cause readmission [OR = 1.38 (95% CI 1.06-1.80), p = 0.02], whereas this was less likely for Group 3 [OR = 0.77 (95% CI 0.58-1.00), p = 0.05].
CONCLUSIONS
Patients receiving ceftaroline more often had favorable clinical responses than those receiving vancomycin or daptomycin monotherapy. In the absence of large-scale randomized controlled trials, these real-world data provide insights into the potential role of ceftaroline for treating MRSA bacteremia.

The Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS) and Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) were used to assess the quality of individual observational and randomized control studies, respectively. Pooled odd ratios were calculated using random effects models.
RESULTS
Twenty studies were included based on a priori set inclusion and exclusion criteria. Daptomycin treatment was associated with non-significant lower mortality odds, compared to vancomycin treatment (OR = 0.81; 95% CI, 0.62, 1.06). Sub-analyses based on the time patients were switched from another anti-MRSA treatment to daptomycin demonstrated that switching to daptomycin within 3 or 5 days was significantly associated with 55% and 45% decreased odds of all-cause mortality, respectively. However, switching to daptomycin any time after five days of treatment was not significantly associated with lower odds of mortality. Stratified analysis based on vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) revealed that daptomycin treatment among patients infected with MRSA strains with MIC≥1 mg/L was significantly associated with 40% lower odds of mortality compared to vancomycin treatment.
CONCLUSION
Compared with vancomycin, an early switch from vancomycin to daptomycin was significantly associated with lower odds of mortality. In contrast, switching to daptomycin at any time only showed a trend towards reduced mortality, with a non-significant association. Therefore, the efficacy of early daptomycin use over vancomycin against mortality among MRSA BSIs patients may add evidence to the existing literature in support of switching to daptomycin early over remaining on vancomycin. More randomized and prospective studies are needed to assess this association.

data.title: Early use of daptomycin versus vancomycin for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia with vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration >1 mg/L: a matched cohort study.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Recent reports have described decreased effectiveness with vancomycin treatment for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (MRSAB) when the vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) is >1 µg/mL.
METHODS
This matched, retrospective cohort study compared the clinical effectiveness of daptomycin with that of vancomycin for the treatment of MRSAB with vancomycin MICs >1 µg/mL. The primary outcome was clinical failure, defined as a composite of 30-day mortality or bacteremia persisting for ≥7 days.
RESULTS
One hundred seventy patients were matched 1:1 with respect to the antimicrobial administered. In the daptomycin group, all patients received <72 hours of vancomycin (median, 1.7 days [interquartile range, 1.1-2.3 days]) prior to switching to daptomycin. The rate of clinical failure at 30 days was significantly lower in the daptomycin arm compared to the vancomycin arm (20.0% vs 48.2%; P < 0.001). Both 30-day mortality and persistent bacteremia were significantly lower in the daptomycin group compared to the vancomycin group (3.5% vs 12.9% [P = .047] and 18.8% vs 42.4% [P = .001], respectively). Logistic regression confirmed the association between vancomycin treatment and increased risk of clinical failure (adjusted odds ratio, 4.5; 95% confidence interval, 2.1-9.8).
CONCLUSIONS
This is the first matched study comparing early daptomycin versus vancomycin for the treatment of MRSAB when the vancomycin MIC is >1 µg/mL. Treatment with daptomycin resulted in significantly improved outcomes, including decreased 30-day mortality and persistent bacteremia. These results support the practice of switching early from vancomycin to daptomycin for the treatment of MRSAB when the vancomycin MIC is >1 µg/mL.

data.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Switching to Daptomycin Versus Remaining on Vancomycin Among Patients With Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Bloodstream Infections.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (MRSA BSI) usually receive initial treatment with vancomycin but may be switched to daptomycin for definitive therapy, especially if treatment failure is suspected. Our objective was to evaluate the effectiveness of switching from vancomycin to daptomycin compared with remaining on vancomycin among patients with MRSA BSI.
METHODS
Patients admitted to 124 Veterans Affairs Hospitals who experienced MRSA BSI and were treated with vancomycin during 2007-2014 were included. The association between switching to daptomycin and 30-day mortality was assessed using Cox regression models. Separate models were created for switching to daptomycin any time during the first hospitalization and for switching within 3 days of receiving vancomycin.
RESULTS
In total, 7411 patients received vancomycin for MRSA BSI. Also, 606 (8.2%) patients switched from vancomycin to daptomycin during the first hospitalization, and 108 (1.5%) switched from vancomycin to daptomycin within 3 days of starting vancomycin. In the multivariable analysis, switching to daptomycin within 3 days was significantly associated with lower 30-day mortality (hazards ratio [HR] = 0.48; 95% confidence interval [CI]: .25, .92). However, switching to daptomycin at any time during the first hospitalization was not significantly associated with 30-day mortality (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: .69, 1.09).
CONCLUSIONS
Switching to daptomycin within 3 days of initial receipt of vancomycin is associated with lower 30-day mortality among patients with MRSA BSI. This benefit was not seen when the switch occurred later. Future studies should prospectively assess the benefit of early switching from vancomycin to other anti-MRSA antibiotics.

data.title: Avoiding the perfect storm: the biologic and clinical case for reevaluating the 7-day expectation for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia before switching therapy.
data.abstract: Persistent methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia (MRSAB) is associated with poor outcomes and serious complications. The MRSA guidelines define treatment failure and persistent bacteremia as lasting ≥7 days; however, this definition requires reevaluation. Aggressively reducing the bacterial inoculum promptly is critical because factors already in place before clinical presentation are driving resistance to the few antibiotics that are available to treat MRSAB. Alternative approaches to treat MRSAB should be considered within 3-4 days of persistent MRSAB. With rapid molecular diagnostics emerging in clinical microbiology laboratories and biomarkers as a potential for early patient risk stratification, a future shorter threshold may become possible.

trajectory.final_answer:
# Bottom line

Early switching from vancomycin to daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia is associated with improved outcomes, particularly when the switch occurs within 3 days of starting vancomycin, whereas switching later does not show a clear mortality benefit. In contrast, among patients who ultimately receive vancomycin, higher vancomycin MICs (>1 µg/mL) are linked to worse outcomes and may warrant consideration of an early switch. However, large randomized trials directly testing early switch strategies are limited, so current evidence is largely from observational cohorts and meta-analyses with potential confounding.

# What the evidence shows

- Observational meta-analysis and large VA cohort data indicate that switching to daptomycin within 3 days of vancomycin initiation is associated with substantially lower 30‑day mortality compared with remaining on vancomycin (hazard ratio ~0.48), while switching at any time later is not significantly associated with mortality benefit. Early timing appears critical. <cite id="38381737,33512521">Switching to daptomycin within 3 days was associated with significantly lower 30‑day mortality, whereas switching later was not; pooled analyses showed early switches (within 3–5 days) reduced all‑cause mortality compared with later or no switching</cite>.

- In a matched cohort of MRSA bacteremia patients with vancomycin MIC >1 µg/mL, early switch to daptomycin (median 1.7 days of prior vancomycin) was associated with markedly lower clinical failure (20% vs 48% at 30 days), lower mortality (3.5% vs 12.9%), and lower persistent bacteremia (18.8% vs 42.4%) compared with continued vancomycin. <cite id="23449272">Among patients with vancomycin MIC >1 µg/mL, early daptomycin switch reduced 30‑day mortality and persistent bacteremia versus vancomycin</cite>.

- Clinical guidance supports reconsidering therapy within 3–4 days in persistent MRSA bacteremia due to the high risk of complications and emerging resistance, aligning with the concept that early switch strategies may improve outcomes when initial therapy is suboptimal. <cite id="25048852">Alternative antibiotics should be considered within 3–4 days in persistent MRSA bacteremia, given the risks of prolonged bacteremia and resistance</cite>.

# Nuances and caveats

- The overall comparative effectiveness of daptomycin versus vancomycin for MRSA BSIs is mixed in observational literature, with some meta-analytic evidence showing no significant difference in mortality when all settings are pooled. However, subgroup analyses highlight that early switches and specific resistance contexts (e.g., vancomycin MIC ≥1 µg/mL) favor daptomycin. <cite id="38381737">Pooled analysis showed non-significant mortality reduction for daptomycin overall, but early switching (within 3–5 days) and high vancomycin MIC subgroups favored daptomycin</cite>.

- There are no definitive randomized trials directly testing "early switch" algorithms between vancomycin and daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia; recommendations remain largely based on observational studies, VA administrative cohorts, and expert reviews. <cite id="38381737,33512521">Authors emphasize the need for randomized and prospective studies to confirm early-switch benefits</cite>.

# Practical implications

- Consider an early switch to daptomycin in patients with MRSA bacteremia who have suboptimal vancomycin exposure (e.g., MIC ≥1 µg/mL), persistent bacteremia, or signs of treatment failure by day 3–4, recognizing the risk of confounding and the need for antimicrobial stewardship. <cite id="23449272,25048852">Early daptomycin switch improved outcomes in MIC >1 µg/mL MRSA bacteremia, and guidelines support reevaluating therapy within 3–4 days when bacteremia persists</cite>.

- If switching, ensure susceptibility of the organism to daptomycin and account for local resistance patterns, renal function, and patient-specific factors. <cite id="38381737">Stratification by vancomycin MIC and timing of switch influenced mortality outcomes</cite>.

# Summary answer

Yes—when done early, switching from vancomycin to daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia is associated with improved clinical outcomes, especially reduced mortality, particularly if the switch occurs within 3 days; later switches do not show consistent benefit. These advantages are most evident in settings of suboptimal vancomycin activity (e.g., MIC >1 µg/mL) or treatment failure, but high-quality randomized trials directly testing early-switch strategies are still needed. <cite id="38381737,33512521,23449272">Early daptomycin switch (within 3–5 days) was associated with lower mortality and clinical failure compared with continued vancomycin, with the greatest benefit when vancomycin MIC is high; later switches were not beneficial</cite>.

<snippet id="32961119">Title: Adjuvant nivolumab versus ipilimumab in resected stage IIIB-C and stage IV melanoma (CheckMate 238): 4-year results from a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial.
Authors: Ascierto, Paolo A, Del Vecchio, Michele, Mandalá, Mario et al. | Year: 2020 | Journal: The Lancet. Oncology
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Previously, findings from CheckMate 238, a double-blind, phase 3 adjuvant trial in patients with resected stage IIIB-C or stage IV melanoma, showed significant improvements in recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival with nivolumab versus ipilimumab. This report provides updated 4-year efficacy, initial overall survival, and late-emergent safety results.
METHODS
This multicentre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial was done in 130 academic centres, community hospitals, and cancer centres across 25 countries. Patients aged 15 years or older with resected stage IIIB-C or IV melanoma and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1 were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive nivolumab or ipilimumab via an interactive voice response system and stratified according to disease stage and baseline PD-L1 status of tumour cells. Patients received intravenous nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks or intravenous ipilimumab 10 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, and then every 12 weeks until 1 year of treatment, disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival by investigator assessment, and overall survival was a key secondary endpoint. Efficacy analyses were done in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients). All patients who received at least one dose of study treatment were included in the safety analysis. The results presented in this report reflect the 4-year update of the ongoing study with a database lock date of Jan 30, 2020. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02388906.
FINDINGS
Between March 30 and Nov 30, 2015, 906 patients were assigned to nivolumab (n=453) or ipilimumab (n=453). Median follow-up was 51·1 months (IQR 41·6-52·7) with nivolumab and 50·9 months (36·2-52·3) with ipilimumab; 4-year recurrence-free survival was 51·7% (95% CI 46·8-56·3) in the nivolumab group and 41·2% (36·4-45·9) in the ipilimumab group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·71 [95% CI 0·60-0·86]; p=0·0003). With 211 (100 [22%] of 453 patients in the nivolumab group and 111 [25%] of 453 patients in the ipilimumab group) of 302 anticipated deaths observed (about 73% of the originally planned 88% power needed for significance), 4-year overall survival was 77·9% (95% CI 73·7-81·5) with nivolumab and 76·6% (72·2-80·3) with ipilimumab (HR 0·87 [95% CI 0·66-1·14]; p=0·31). Late-emergent grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were reported in three (1%) of 452 and seven (2%) of 453 patients. The most common late-emergent treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events reported were diarrhoea, diabetic ketoacidosis, and pneumonitis (one patient each) in the nivolumab group, and colitis (two patients) in the ipilimumab group. Two previously reported treatment-related deaths in the ipilimumab group were attributed to study drug toxicity (marrow aplasia in one patient and colitis in one patient); no further treatment-related deaths were reported.
INTERPRETATION
At a minimum of 4 years' follow-up, nivolumab demonstrated sustained recurrence-free survival benefit versus ipilimumab in resected stage IIIB-C or IV melanoma indicating a long-term treatment benefit with nivolumab. With fewer deaths than anticipated, overall survival was similar in both groups. Nivolumab remains an efficacious adjuvant treatment for patients with resected high-risk melanoma, with a safety profile that is more tolerable than that of ipilimumab.

Bristol Myers Squibb and Ono Pharmaceutical.</snippet>

<snippet id="26027431">Title: Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab or Monotherapy in Untreated Melanoma.
Authors: Larkin, James, Chiarion-Sileni, Vanna, Gonzalez, Rene et al. | Year: 2015 | Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Nivolumab (a programmed death 1 [PD-1] checkpoint inhibitor) and ipilimumab (a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 [CTLA-4] checkpoint inhibitor) have been shown to have complementary activity in metastatic melanoma. In this randomized, double-blind, phase 3 study, nivolumab alone or nivolumab plus ipilimumab was compared with ipilimumab alone in patients with metastatic melanoma.
METHODS
We assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, 945 previously untreated patients with unresectable stage III or IV melanoma to nivolumab alone, nivolumab plus ipilimumab, or ipilimumab alone. Progression-free survival and overall survival were coprimary end points. Results regarding progression-free survival are presented here.
RESULTS
The median progression-free survival was 11.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 8.9 to 16.7) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, as compared with 2.9 months (95% CI, 2.8 to 3.4) with ipilimumab (hazard ratio for death or disease progression, 0.42; 99.5% CI, 0.31 to 0.57; P<0.001), and 6.9 months (95% CI, 4.3 to 9.5) with nivolumab (hazard ratio for the comparison with ipilimumab, 0.57; 99.5% CI, 0.43 to 0.76; P<0.001). In patients with tumors positive for the PD-1 ligand (PD-L1), the median progression-free survival was 14.0 months in the nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab group and in the nivolumab group, but in patients with PD-L1-negative tumors, progression-free survival was longer with the combination therapy than with nivolumab alone (11.2 months [95% CI, 8.0 to not reached] vs. 5.3 months [95% CI, 2.8 to 7.1]). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or 4 occurred in 16.3% of the patients in the nivolumab group, 55.0% of those in the nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab group, and 27.3% of those in the ipilimumab group.
CONCLUSIONS
Among previously untreated patients with metastatic melanoma, nivolumab alone or combined with ipilimumab resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival than ipilimumab alone. In patients with PD-L1-negative tumors, the combination of PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade was more effective than either agent alone. (Funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb; CheckMate 067 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT01844505.).</snippet>
<snippet id="30361170">Title: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone versus ipilimumab alone in advanced melanoma (CheckMate 067): 4-year outcomes of a multicentre, randomised, phase 3 trial.
Authors: Hodi, Frank Stephen, Chiarion-Sileni, Vanna, Gonzalez, Rene et al. | Year: 2018 | Journal: The Lancet. Oncology
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Previously reported results from the phase 3 CheckMate 067 trial showed a significant improvement in objective responses, progression-free survival, and overall survival with nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone compared with ipilimumab alone in patients with advanced melanoma. The aim of this report is to provide 4-year updated efficacy and safety data from this study.
METHODS
In this phase 3 trial, eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with previously untreated, unresectable, stage III or stage IV melanoma, known BRAF V600 mutation status, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to receive intravenous nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, followed by nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks, or nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus placebo, or ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses plus placebo. Randomisation was done via an interactive voice response system with a permuted block schedule (block size of six) and stratification by PD-L1 status, BRAF mutation status, and metastasis stage. The patients, investigators, study site staff, and study funder were masked to the study drug administered. The co-primary endpoints were progression-free survival and overall survival. Efficacy analyses were done on the intention-to-treat population, whereas safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study drug. The results presented in this report reflect the 4-year update of the ongoing study with a database lock date of May 10, 2018. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT01844505.
FINDINGS
Between July 3, 2013, and March 31, 2014, 945 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n=314), nivolumab (n=316), or ipilimumab (n=315). Median follow-up was 46·9 months (IQR 10·9-51·8) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group, 36·0 months (10·5-51·4) in the nivolumab group, and 18·6 months (7·6-49·5) in the ipilimumab group. At a minimum follow-up of 48 months from the date that the final patient was enrolled and randomised, median overall survival was not reached (95% CI 38·2-not reached) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group, 36·9 months (28·3-not reached) in the nivolumab group, and 19·9 months (16·9-24·6) in the ipilimumab group. The hazard ratio for death for the combination versus ipilimumab was 0·54 (95% CI 0·44-0·67; p<0·0001) and for nivolumab versus ipilimumab was 0·65 (0·53-0·79; p<0·0001). Median progression-free survival was 11·5 months (95% CI 8·7-19·3) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group, 6·9 months (5·1-10·2) in the nivolumab group, and 2·9 months (2·8-3·2) in the ipilimumab group. The hazard ratio for progression-free survival for the combination versus ipilimumab was 0·42 (95% CI 0·35-0·51; p<0·0001) and for nivolumab versus ipilimumab was 0·53 (0·44-0·64; p<0·0001). Treatment-related grade 3-4 adverse events were reported in 185 (59%) of 313 patients who received nivolumab plus ipilimumab, 70 (22%) of 313 who received nivolumab, and 86 (28%) of 311 who received ipilimumab. The most common treatment-related grade 3 adverse events were diarrhoea in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group (29 [9%] of 313) and in the nivolumab group (nine [3%] of 313) and colitis in the ipilimumab group (23 [7%] of 311); the most common grade 4 adverse event in all three groups was increased lipase (15 [5%] of 313 in the combination group, ten [3%] of 313 in the nivolumab group, and four [1%] of 311 in the ipilimumab group). Serious adverse events were not analysed for the 4-year follow-up. In total for the study, there were four treatment-related deaths: two in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group (one cardiomyopathy and one liver necrosis), one in the nivolumab group (neutropenia), and one in the ipilimumab group (colon perforation). No additional treatment-related deaths have occurred since the previous (3-year) analysis.
INTERPRETATION
The results of this analysis at 4 years of follow-up show that a durable, sustained survival benefit can be achieved with first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone in patients with advanced melanoma.
FUNDING
Bristol-Myers Squibb.</snippet>

data.title: Adjuvant nivolumab versus ipilimumab in resected stage IIIB-C and stage IV melanoma (CheckMate 238): 4-year results from a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Previously, findings from CheckMate 238, a double-blind, phase 3 adjuvant trial in patients with resected stage IIIB-C or stage IV melanoma, showed significant improvements in recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival with nivolumab versus ipilimumab. This report provides updated 4-year efficacy, initial overall survival, and late-emergent safety results.
METHODS
This multicentre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial was done in 130 academic centres, community hospitals, and cancer centres across 25 countries. Patients aged 15 years or older with resected stage IIIB-C or IV melanoma and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1 were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive nivolumab or ipilimumab via an interactive voice response system and stratified according to disease stage and baseline PD-L1 status of tumour cells. Patients received intravenous nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks or intravenous ipilimumab 10 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, and then every 12 weeks until 1 year of treatment, disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival by investigator assessment, and overall survival was a key secondary endpoint. Efficacy analyses were done in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients). All patients who received at least one dose of study treatment were included in the safety analysis. The results presented in this report reflect the 4-year update of the ongoing study with a database lock date of Jan 30, 2020. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02388906.
FINDINGS
Between March 30 and Nov 30, 2015, 906 patients were assigned to nivolumab (n=453) or ipilimumab (n=453). Median follow-up was 51·1 months (IQR 41·6-52·7) with nivolumab and 50·9 months (36·2-52·3) with ipilimumab; 4-year recurrence-free survival was 51·7% (95% CI 46·8-56·3) in the nivolumab group and 41·2% (36·4-45·9) in the ipilimumab group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·71 [95% CI 0·60-0·86]; p=0·0003). With 211 (100 [22%] of 453 patients in the nivolumab group and 111 [25%] of 453 patients in the ipilimumab group) of 302 anticipated deaths observed (about 73% of the originally planned 88% power needed for significance), 4-year overall survival was 77·9% (95% CI 73·7-81·5) with nivolumab and 76·6% (72·2-80·3) with ipilimumab (HR 0·87 [95% CI 0·66-1·14]; p=0·31). Late-emergent grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were reported in three (1%) of 452 and seven (2%) of 453 patients. The most common late-emergent treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events reported were diarrhoea, diabetic ketoacidosis, and pneumonitis (one patient each) in the nivolumab group, and colitis (two patients) in the ipilimumab group. Two previously reported treatment-related deaths in the ipilimumab group were attributed to study drug toxicity (marrow aplasia in one patient and colitis in one patient); no further treatment-related deaths were reported.
INTERPRETATION
At a minimum of 4 years' follow-up, nivolumab demonstrated sustained recurrence-free survival benefit versus ipilimumab in resected stage IIIB-C or IV melanoma indicating a long-term treatment benefit with nivolumab. With fewer deaths than anticipated, overall survival was similar in both groups. Nivolumab remains an efficacious adjuvant treatment for patients with resected high-risk melanoma, with a safety profile that is more tolerable than that of ipilimumab.
FUNDING
Bristol Myers Squibb and Ono Pharmaceutical.

data.title: Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab or Monotherapy in Untreated Melanoma.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Nivolumab (a programmed death 1 [PD-1] checkpoint inhibitor) and ipilimumab (a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 [CTLA-4] checkpoint inhibitor) have been shown to have complementary activity in metastatic melanoma. In this randomized, double-blind, phase 3 study, nivolumab alone or nivolumab plus ipilimumab was compared with ipilimumab alone in patients with metastatic melanoma.
METHODS
We assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, 945 previously untreated patients with unresectable stage III or IV melanoma to nivolumab alone, nivolumab plus ipilimumab, or ipilimumab alone. Progression-free survival and overall survival were coprimary end points. Results regarding progression-free survival are presented here.
RESULTS
The median progression-free survival was 11.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 8.9 to 16.7) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, as compared with 2.9 months (95% CI, 2.8 to 3.4) with ipilimumab (hazard ratio for death or disease progression, 0.42; 99.5% CI, 0.31 to 0.57; P<0.001), and 6.9 months (95% CI, 4.3 to 9.5) with nivolumab (hazard ratio for the comparison with ipilimumab, 0.57; 99.5% CI, 0.43 to 0.76; P<0.001). In patients with tumors positive for the PD-1 ligand (PD-L1), the median progression-free survival was 14.0 months in the nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab group and in the nivolumab group, but in patients with PD-L1-negative tumors, progression-free survival was longer with the combination therapy than with nivolumab alone (11.2 months [95% CI, 8.0 to not reached] vs. 5.3 months [95% CI, 2.8 to 7.1]). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or 4 occurred in 16.3% of the patients in the nivolumab group, 55.0% of those in the nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab group, and 27.3% of those in the ipilimumab group.
CONCLUSIONS
Among previously untreated patients with metastatic melanoma, nivolumab alone or combined with ipilimumab resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival than ipilimumab alone. In patients with PD-L1-negative tumors, the combination of PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade was more effective than either agent alone. (Funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb; CheckMate 067 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT01844505.).

data.title: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone versus ipilimumab alone in advanced melanoma (CheckMate 067): 4-year outcomes of a multicentre, randomised, phase 3 trial.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Previously reported results from the phase 3 CheckMate 067 trial showed a significant improvement in objective responses, progression-free survival, and overall survival with nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone compared with ipilimumab alone in patients with advanced melanoma. The aim of this report is to provide 4-year updated efficacy and safety data from this study.
METHODS
In this phase 3 trial, eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with previously untreated, unresectable, stage III or stage IV melanoma, known BRAF V600 mutation status, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to receive intravenous nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, followed by nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks, or nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus placebo, or ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses plus placebo. Randomisation was done via an interactive voice response system with a permuted block schedule (block size of six) and stratification by PD-L1 status, BRAF mutation status, and metastasis stage. The patients, investigators, study site staff, and study funder were masked to the study drug administered. The co-primary endpoints were progression-free survival and overall survival. Efficacy analyses were done on the intention-to-treat population, whereas safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study drug. The results presented in this report reflect the 4-year update of the ongoing study with a database lock date of May 10, 2018. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT01844505.
FINDINGS
Between July 3, 2013, and March 31, 2014, 945 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n=314), nivolumab (n=316), or ipilimumab (n=315). Median follow-up was 46·9 months (IQR 10·9-51·8) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group, 36·0 months (10·5-51·4) in the nivolumab group, and 18·6 months (7·6-49·5) in the ipilimumab group. At a minimum follow-up of 48 months from the date that the final patient was enrolled and randomised, median overall survival was not reached (95% CI 38·2-not reached) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group, 36·9 months (28·3-not reached) in the nivolumab group, and 19·9 months (16·9-24·6) in the ipilimumab group. The hazard ratio for death for the combination versus ipilimumab was 0·54 (95% CI 0·44-0·67; p<0·0001) and for nivolumab versus ipilimumab was 0·65 (0·53-0·79; p<0·0001). Median progression-free survival was 11·5 months (95% CI 8·7-19·3) in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group, 6·9 months (5·1-10·2) in the nivolumab group, and 2·9 months (2·8-3·2) in the ipilimumab group. The hazard ratio for progression-free survival for the combination versus ipilimumab was 0·42 (95% CI 0·35-0·51; p<0·0001) and for nivolumab versus ipilimumab was 0·53 (0·44-0·64; p<0·0001). Treatment-related grade 3-4 adverse events were reported in 185 (59%) of 313 patients who received nivolumab plus ipilimumab, 70 (22%) of 313 who received nivolumab, and 86 (28%) of 311 who received ipilimumab. The most common treatment-related grade 3 adverse events were diarrhoea in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group (29 [9%] of 313) and in the nivolumab group (nine [3%] of 313) and colitis in the ipilimumab group (23 [7%] of 311); the most common grade 4 adverse event in all three groups was increased lipase (15 [5%] of 313 in the combination group, ten [3%] of 313 in the nivolumab group, and four [1%] of 311 in the ipilimumab group). Serious adverse events were not analysed for the 4-year follow-up. In total for the study, there were four treatment-related deaths: two in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group (one cardiomyopathy and one liver necrosis), one in the nivolumab group (neutropenia), and one in the ipilimumab group (colon perforation). No additional treatment-related deaths have occurred since the previous (3-year) analysis.
INTERPRETATION
The results of this analysis at 4 years of follow-up show that a durable, sustained survival benefit can be achieved with first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone in patients with advanced melanoma.
FUNDING
Bristol-Myers Squibb.

data.title: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum for metastatic nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer: KEYNOTE-189 Japan Study.
data.abstract: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum significantly improved overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) with manageable safety compared with placebo plus pemetrexed-platinum in patients with previously untreated metastatic nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without EGFR/ALK alterations in the global, randomized, double-blind, phase 3 KEYNOTE-189 study. We present results of Japanese patients enrolled in the KEYNOTE-189 global and Japan extension studies. Patients were randomized 2:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks (Q3W) for up to 35 cycles. All patients received pemetrexed 500 mg/m 2 plus the investigator's choice of cisplatin or carboplatin Q3W for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed 500 mg/m 2 Q3W (all intravenous). Co-primary endpoints were OS and PFS. Forty Japanese patients enrolled (pembrolizumab, n = 25; placebo, n = 15). At data cutoff (20 May 2019; median time from randomization to data cutoff, 18.5 [range, 14.7-38.2] months), the median OS was not reached in the pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum arm; the median OS was 25.9 (95% confidence interval [CI], 11.9-29.0) months in the placebo plus pemetrexed-platinum arm (hazard ratio [HR] .29; 95% CI, .07-1.15). The median (95% CI) PFS was 16.5 (8.8-21.1) compared with 7.1 (4.7-21.4) months (HR, .62; 95% CI, .27-1.42), respectively. There were no grade 5 adverse events (AE). Grade 3/4 AE occurred in 72% vs 60% of patients in the pembrolizumab vs placebo arms; 40% vs 20% had immune-mediated AE, and 4% vs 0% had infusion reactions. Efficacy and safety outcomes were similar to those from the global study and support first-line therapy with pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in Japanese patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without EGFR/ALK alterations.

<snippet id="29599079">Title: Efficient In Vivo Liver-Directed Gene Editing Using CRISPR/Cas9.
Authors: Singh, Kshitiz, Evens, Hanneke, Nair, Nisha et al. | Year: 2018 | Journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
Abstract: In vivo tissue-specific genome editing at the desired loci is still a challenge. Here, we report that AAV9-delivery of truncated guide RNAs (gRNAs) and Cas9 under the control of a computationally designed hepatocyte-specific promoter lead to liver-specific and sequence-specific targeting in the mouse factor IX (F9) gene. The efficiency of in vivo targeting was assessed by T7E1 assays, site-specific Sanger sequencing, and deep sequencing of on-target and putative off-target sites. Though AAV9 transduction was apparent in multiple tissues and organs, Cas9 expression was restricted mainly to the liver, with only minimal or no expression in other non-hepatic tissues. Consequently, the insertions and deletion (indel) frequency was robust in the liver (up to 50%) in the desired target loci of the F9 gene, with no evidence of targeting in other organs or other putative off-target sites. This resulted in a substantial loss of FIX activity and the emergence of a bleeding phenotype, consistent with hemophilia B. The in vivo efficacy of the truncated gRNA was as high as that of full-length gRNA. Cas9 expression was transient in neonates, representing an attractive "hit-and-run" paradigm. Our findings have potentially broad implications for somatic gene targeting in the liver using the CRISPR/Cas9 platform.</snippet>

- AAV vectors engineered for hepatocyte specificity can reach high on-target rates in liver tissue. - With careful promoter restriction and truncated gRNA use, AAV-delivered CRISPR in the liver showed no detectable off-target targeting in other organs or at surveyed putative off-target sites, consistent with hepatocyte-restricted Cas9 expression and a "hit-and-run" strategy that limits duration of nuclease activity <cite id="29599079">Cas9 expression was restricted mainly to the liver, with minimal/no expression in other tissues; no evidence of targeting in other organs or other putative off-target sites; transient Cas9 in neonates</cite>.

# Innate Immune Activation

- AAV-mediated liver-directed editing with hepatocyte-specific promoters and truncated gRNAs minimized extra-hepatic expression and employed transient Cas9 expression, which are strategies that can dampen innate immune responses by limiting nuclease exposure.
