trajectory.final_answer:
# Summary

Gut microbiome-derived metabolites, particularly short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and bile acids, influence host metabolism through multiple mechanisms that can improve insulin sensitivity and alter liver fat and fibrosis in adults. SCFAs produced by colonic fermentation (acetate, propionate, butyrate) modulate appetite, incretin hormone secretion, energy substrate oxidation, inflammation, and oxidative stress, with human randomized trials showing improvements in insulin sensitivity and reductions in intrahepatocellular lipid when colonic propionate is increased. Bile acids activate farnesoid X receptor (FXR) and TGR5 pathways; in NAFLD/NASH, pharmacologic modulation (FXR agonism or bile acid synthesis inhibition) improves histologic activity and fibrosis and improves metabolic markers including bile acids and insulin, though FXR agonists can cause pruritus. Overall, these data support a role for microbiome-derived metabolites as modulators of glucose homeostasis and NAFLD severity, with translational potential and safety considerations that are now clearer from randomized trials.

# Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs): effects on glucose homeostasis

- Propionate delivery to the human colon improves insulin sensitivity in adults with overweight/obesity in a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial, with distinct effects on plasma metabolome and systemic inflammation compared with fermentable vs. non-fermentable fiber controls. Improvements in HOMA2-IR were seen with both inulin-propionate ester (IPE) and inulin, but IPE uniquely reduced IL-8 and altered bacterial classes/orders, indicating a propionate-specific signature on metabolic and inflammatory remodeling. <cite id="30971437">Both IPE and inulin supplementation improved insulin resistance compared with cellulose, with distinct effects on plasma metabolome, gut bacterial populations, and inflammatory markers, and IPE decreased interleukin-8 compared with cellulose.</cite>

- Targeted colonic propionate raises gut hormone signaling and reduces appetite, which can favorably impact weight and insulin sensitivity. In human cell models and acute crossover studies, propionate stimulated PYY and GLP-1 release, increased postprandial PYY after ingestion, and reduced energy intake; over 24 weeks, daily IPE prevented deterioration in insulin sensitivity and reduced intra-abdominal adipose tissue and intrahepatocellular lipid versus control. <cite id="25500202">Propionate stimulated PYY and GLP-1 secretion in human colonic cells, acutely increased postprandial PYY and GLP-1 and reduced energy intake after ingestion, and over 24 weeks reduced weight gain, intra-abdominal adipose tissue, intrahepatocellular lipid, and prevented deterioration in insulin sensitivity versus inulin control.</cite>

- SCFA mixtures administered rectally in overweight/obese men increased fasting fat oxidation, raised resting energy expenditure, and increased fasting and postprandial PYY, while attenuating fasting free glycerol (lipolysis), indicating improved substrate partitioning and hormonal milieu supportive of glucose control. <cite id="28539646">Colonic SCFA infusions increased fasting fat oxidation, raised resting energy expenditure after acetate and propionate versus placebo, increased fasting and postprandial PYY, and attenuated fasting free glycerol, suggesting decreased lipolysis and improved substrate metabolism.</cite>

- Diet-mediated increases in specific SCFAs can reduce oxidative stress, a contributor to insulin resistance. In adults with abdominal obesity and metabolic risk, an aleurone-rich wheat diet increased postprandial butyrate and inversely correlated butyrate at 180 min with urinary 8-isoprostane (a biomarker of oxidative stress), suggesting a mechanism by which SCFAs may improve insulin sensitivity. <cite id="41156541">A wheat aleurone–rich diet increased postprandial butyrate and showed an inverse correlation between butyrate at 180 min and urinary 8-isoprostane, indicating lower oxidative stress.</cite>

- Whole-grain vs. refined-grain diets did not significantly change insulin sensitivity or plasma SCFAs in a randomized cross-over trial, but reduced body weight and low-grade inflammation, highlighting that not all diet-induced microbiome shifts translate directly to glucose improvements and that inflammatory pathways may mediate benefits. <cite id="29097438">A whole grain diet reduced body weight and serum IL-6 and CRP but did not significantly alter glucose homeostasis or plasma short-chain fatty acids or major fecal microbiome features versus refined grain.</cite>

Overall, human data indicate SCFAs can enhance insulin sensitivity and metabolic flexibility via gut hormone signaling, reduced lipolysis, and lower oxidative stress, with propionate and butyrate showing the most consistent beneficial signals in adults.

# SCFAs and NAFLD/steatosis

- Propionate delivery and sustained SCFA signaling reduce hepatic fat and preserve insulin sensitivity in overweight adults, suggesting potential benefits for NAFLD severity. Over 24 weeks, increasing colonic propionate prevented worsening insulin sensitivity and reduced intrahepatocellular lipid and intra-abdominal adipose tissue, which are central to NAFLD progression. <cite id="25500202">Increasing colonic propionate via IPE over 24 weeks reduced intra-hepatocellular lipid and prevented deterioration in insulin sensitivity compared with inulin control in overweight adults.</cite>

- Beyond surrogate markers, SCFA infusions modulate energy substrate oxidation and appetite, which can indirectly mitigate NAFLD risk factors by reducing adiposity and ectopic fat. In overweight/obese men, acetate-, propionate-, and butyrate-rich infusions increased fat oxidation and energy expenditure and increased PYY, consistent with reduced energy intake and improved lipid handling. <cite id="28539646">SCFA infusions increased fat oxidation and energy expenditure and elevated PYY, supporting improved energy partitioning relevant to NAFLD risk.</cite>

- Diet-induced increases in butyrate associate with lower oxidative stress in adults with cardio-metabolic risk, which may reduce lipotoxicity and inflammation in the liver. The inverse link between postprandial butyrate and oxidative stress markers supports a plausible mechanism for mitigating NAFLD progression. <cite id="41156541">Higher postprandial butyrate after a wheat aleurone diet correlated inversely with oxidative stress, suggesting a mechanism by which SCFAs may ameliorate liver injury.</cite>

Collectively, SCFAs appear to attenuate NAFLD severity through improved insulin sensitivity, reduced lipolysis and adiposity, and anti-inflammatory/anti-oxidative effects, though direct histologic regression data in adults remain limited compared to pharmacologic bile acid modulation.

# Bile acids, FXR/TGR5 signaling, and NAFLD/insulin resistance

- FXR agonism with obeticholic acid (OCA) improves histologic NASH features in adults with F2–F3 fibrosis, with greater fibrosis improvement at higher doses, albeit with dose-related pruritus. In a large randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 interim analysis, OCA 25 mg increased the probability of ≥1-stage fibrosis improvement without NASH worsening versus placebo, while NASH resolution did not significantly change; adverse events, particularly pruritus, were dose-related. <cite id="31813633">Obeticholic acid 25 mg significantly increased fibrosis improvement without NASH worsening versus placebo in adults with NASH and F2–F3 fibrosis, while NASH resolution did not improve; pruritus incidence was dose-related and generally mild to moderate.</cite>

- Nonsteroidal FXR agonism (cilofexor) reduces hepatic steatosis and serum bile acids and improves liver biochemistry in noncirrhotic NASH, supporting antilipotoxic and anti-inflammatory effects. In a 24-week phase 2 trial, cilofexor 100 mg produced a median -22.7% decrease in MRI-PDFF versus +1.9% with placebo, with higher rates of ≥30% steatosis reduction; cilofexor also lowered gamma-GGT, C4, and primary bile acids. <cite id="32115759">Cilofexor 100 mg for 24 weeks reduced hepatic fat fraction by 22.7% versus an increase of 1.9% with placebo, decreased serum gamma-GGT, C4, and primary bile acids, and was generally well tolerated with pruritus more common at 100 mg than 30 mg.</cite>

- Combining a bile acid synthesis inhibitor (firsocostat) with an FXR agonist (cilofexor) improves histologic activity and biochemical markers in patients with advanced NASH, including reductions in bile acids and improvements in insulin, kidney function, and liver stiffness. In a 48-week phase 2b trial in bridging fibrosis/cirrhosis, the cilofexor/firsocostat combination achieved the primary histologic endpoint more than placebo and improved steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, ALT/AST, bilirubin, bile acids, insulin, and liver stiffness. <cite id="33169409">Cilofexor plus firsocostat increased the proportion achieving ≥1-stage fibrosis improvement without NASH worsening versus placebo and improved steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, ALT/AST, bilirubin, bile acids, insulin, estimated GFR, ELF score, and liver stiffness.</cite>

- In broader metabolic contexts, FXR activation influences lipoprotein metabolism; in NASH patients, OCA raises LDL cholesterol and LDL particle concentration acutely, but these changes are mitigated by statins, underscoring the need to manage cardiometabolic risks when modulating bile acid signaling. <cite id="31402538">Obeticholic acid increased LDL cholesterol and LDL particle concentration at week 4, which were mitigated by concurrent atorvastatin, and the combination was generally safe and well tolerated.</cite>

- Beyond FXR, modulation of bile acid enterohepatic circulation and downstream signaling can improve insulin sensitivity and NAFLD features. In NASH, cilofexor/firsocostat reduced bile acids and improved insulin and other metabolic markers, consistent with bile acid–mediated effects on insulin resistance and hepatic inflammation. <cite id="33169409">Bile acid–targeted therapy (cilofexor/firsocostat) improved insulin and other metabolic markers in addition to histology, supporting bile acid signaling as a lever for metabolic and liver benefit.</cite>

# Safety and translational considerations

- FXR agonists (OCA, cilofexor) can cause pruritus, with incidence increasing with dose and treatment duration; benefits on histology must be balanced against tolerability and potential extr hepatic metabolic effects (e.g., lipids). <cite id="31813633">Pruritus was dose-related with obeticholic acid (up to 51% at 25 mg), with overall safety similar across groups and serious adverse events comparable to placebo.</cite> <cite id="32115759">Pruritus was more common with cilofexor 100 mg than with lower doses or placebo, and higher doses did not provide additional benefits.</cite> <cite id="31402538">Combining OCA with atorvastatin mitigated adverse lipid effects of OCA, supporting risk management in patients with cardiometabolic comorbidity.</cite>

- Diet- and fiber-based strategies to raise SCFAs can improve insulin sensitivity and reduce inflammation, but effects on glucose homeostasis are diet- and dose-dependent; not all interventions change insulin sensitivity or SCFAs in plasma, emphasizing that target tissue exposure (e.g., hepatic vs. systemic) and metabolite specificity (acetate vs. propionate vs. butyrate) may determine outcomes. <cite id="30971437">IPE and inulin improved insulin resistance with distinct plasma metabolomic signatures, while IPE uniquely reduced IL-8.</cite> <cite id="29097438">A whole grain diet reduced body weight and inflammation without altering insulin sensitivity or plasma SCFAs, indicating indirect pathways to metabolic benefit.</cite>

# Evidence gaps and future directions

- Direct, long-term human evidence linking SCFAs to histologic NAFLD improvement (steatosis, lobular inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis) is limited to surrogate endpoints and short interventions; longer trials measuring MRI-PDFF, MRE stiffness, and liver biopsy with SCFA modulation (e.g., targeted fiber, prebiotics, or synbiotics) are needed. <cite id="25500202">Propionate increased for 24 weeks reduced intra-hepatocellular lipid and preserved insulin sensitivity, but histologic endpoints were not reported.</cite> <cite id="28539646">SCFA infusions improved substrate metabolism but were short-term interventions.</cite>

- Personalized responses to bile acid modulation may depend on baseline FXR/TGR5 signaling, genetic background, and comorbidities; stratifying patients by bile acid profiles, pruritus risk, and lipid outcomes could optimize therapy. <cite id="31813633">FXR agonism improved histology but with dose-related pruritus, suggesting a need for patient selection and monitoring.</cite> <cite id="31402538">OCA’s lipid effects highlight the importance of co-therapies to manage cardiometabolic risk.</cite>

# Practical implications

- Increasing colonic SCFA production via fermentable fibers, targeted delivery (e.g., IPE), or diet components that preferentially raise butyrate may improve insulin sensitivity and reduce oxidative stress and liver fat, offering a non-invasive strategy to mitigate glucose dysregulation and early NAFLD. <cite id="30971437">Fiber supplementation improved insulin resistance with distinct microbiome and metabolome signatures.</cite> <cite id="41156541">A wheat aleurone–rich diet increased postprandial butyrate and lowered oxidative stress markers.</cite>

- For adults with established NASH/advanced fibrosis, bile acid pathway modulation (FXR agonists or bile acid synthesis inhibitors) can improve histologic activity and metabolic parameters, but requires careful monitoring for pruritus and lipid changes. <cite id="31813633">Obeticholic acid improved fibrosis without worsening NASH at 25 mg in F2–F3 NASH, with pruritus as the main adverse effect.</cite> <cite id="33169409">Cilofexor plus firsocostat improved histology and metabolic markers including bile acids and insulin in advanced NASH.</cite>

# Conclusion

Gut microbiome-derived metabolites play biologically plausible and, in several cases, clinically supported roles in modulating glucose homeostasis and NAFLD severity in adults. SCFAs enhance insulin sensitivity and metabolic flexibility and may reduce hepatic fat and oxidative stress, while bile acid–mediated FXR/TGR5 signaling can improve NAFLD histology and metabolic parameters when therapeutically modulated, albeit with pruritus and lipid effects that require management. Continued work to optimize delivery, personalize treatment, and extend diet-based strategies into histologic endpoints will clarify causal pathways and maximize clinical benefit. <cite id="30971437,25500202,28539646,41156541,29097438,31813633,33169409,32115759,31402538">SCFAs and bile acids modulate glucose homeostasis and NAFLD severity in adults through effects on insulin sensitivity, appetite and incretin hormones, substrate oxidation, inflammation and oxidative stress, and nuclear receptor signaling, with translational support from randomized human trials and mechanistic readouts, alongside safety considerations such as pruritus and lipid changes.</cite>
